item.title: Diagnostic performance and testing costs of pooled testing for molecular detection of tuberculosis in seven countries: a prospective, observational, diagnostic accuracy study.
item.author: Garg T, Sander M, Byrne RL, Rahman SMM, Santos VS, Wandiga S, Choko AT, Abdulkarim S, Iwakun MO, Codlin AJ, Kontogianni K, Iem V, Cubas Atienzar AI, Henrion MYR, Squire SB, Banu S, Mbuli C, Okumu AO, Bimba J, John S, Vo LNQ, Wingfield T, Creswell J, Start4All Investigators.
item.description:
Background Globally in 2024, only 54% of people diagnosed with tuberculosis received an initial WHO-recommended rapid molecular diagnostic test. Pooled testing could expand access to molecular detection using existing laboratory capacity. We aimed to evaluate the performance of pooled tuberculosis testing in a multicentre diagnostic accuracy study. Methods In this prospective diagnostic accuracy study, we enrolled individuals with presumptive tuberculosis through facility-based case finding (district hospitals and primary health centres) and community-based case finding in Bangladesh, Brazil, Cameroon, Kenya, Malawi, Nigeria, and Viet Nam between Nov 30, 2023, and Feb 27, 2025. item.title: Mortality and disability after hospitalisation for injuries in low-income and middle-income countries: a cohort study.
item.author: Equi-Injury Group.
item.description:
Background Mortality and disability after injuries are high in low-income and middle-income countries (LMICs). Improving outcomes for injured patients requires knowledge of their associated factors. We aimed to assess post-injury mortality and disability and their associations with access to health care across LMICs with different injury burdens, health-care systems, and contexts. Methods Hospitalised patients in Ghana, Pakistan, Rwanda, and South Africa with moderate-to-severe injuries were recruited and followed up until 3 months after discharge or death. Injured patients of any age who were admitted to facilities for more than 12 h or died within 12 h of admission were included. Data were collected between Feb 17, 2023, and Aug 31, 2024, using the REDCap electronic data platform. item.title: HIV service delivery after the PEPFAR and USAID HIV funding withdrawal in Uganda and Zimbabwe: an interrupted time-series study.
item.author: Cust H, Chabata ST, Partners in Uganda and Zimbabwe.
item.description:
Background In January 2025, the US Government froze foreign aid and halted the President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR), the largest external funder of HIV services globally. Early modelling studies and rapid assessments warned of major harm to millions, but robust quantitative evidence from those who relied most on the lost funding has been absent. We aimed to estimate the effect of the US funding withdrawal on HIV prevention, pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), testing, and treatment services provided by non-governmental organisations (NGOs) serving primarily key populations in Uganda and Zimbabwe. item.title: Global, regional, and national burden of exposure to chewing tobacco, 1990-2023: a systematic analysis of the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.
item.author: GBD 2023 Chewing Tobacco Collaborators.
item.description:
Background Exposure to chewing tobacco is a known health risk factor but has received less attention than smoking in global tobacco control efforts. As the evidence base linking chewing tobacco use to poor health grows, it is essential to closely track the changing use of chewing tobacco distinct from other forms of smokeless tobacco, as well as the estimated burden associated with its use. These data are essential to inform policy makers who seek to identify and avert the health burden associated with these dangerous products. Methods We estimated the prevalence of chewing tobacco use and attributable health burden for individuals aged 15 years and older across 204 countries and territories by age and sex to produce temporal estimates from 1990 to 2023 as part of the Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study 2023. item.title: 2022 WHO estimates for overall and human papillomavirus test-based cervical cancer screening coverage worldwide: a review and synthetic analysis.
item.author: Serrano B, Roura E, Alemany L, de Sanjose S, Cowan M, Poljak M, Murillo R, Herrero R, Arbyn M, Almonte M, Ilbawi A, Riley LM, Bruni L.
item.description:
Background Regularly updated global estimates are needed to monitor progress in cervical cancer screening, a key pillar of WHO's strategy to eliminate cervical cancer. We aimed to update estimates of cervical cancer screening coverage in 194 WHO member states and eight associated countries and territories for 2022, including the first global assessment of human papillomavirus (HPV) test-based screening adoption and roll-out. Methods In this review and synthetic analysis, we used an established method to estimate standardised cervical cancer screening coverage in 2022. We used programme and population-based coverage data collected up to Jan 31, 2024, selecting the sources considered most representative of each country or territory's screening situation in 2022.
